About the Role

We are seeking a motivated and analytical ICT Business and Systems Analyst to join our growing team. In this role, you will work closely with business stakeholders to understand operational requirements, analyse existing systems, and deliver technology solutions that improve efficiency, productivity, and business performance.

You will act as the bridge between business needs and technical implementation by gathering requirements, documenting processes, and supporting the successful delivery of ICT projects.

Key Responsibilities

Consult with stakeholders to identify business needs and system requirements.
Analyse current business processes and recommend technology-driven improvements.
Gather, document and validate functional and technical requirements.
Prepare business requirement documents, process maps, user stories and functional specifications.
Work closely with software developers, project managers and third-party vendors to implement solutions.
Perform system testing, user acceptance testing (UAT) and quality assurance activities.
Assist with system integration, deployment and post-implementation support.
Analyse data and prepare reports to support business decision-making.
Develop user documentation, training materials and standard operating procedures.
Identify opportunities for process automation and digital transformation.
Monitor system performance and recommend ongoing improvements.
Ensure solutions comply with organisational policies, security requirements and industry best practices.

Skills & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Information Systems or a related discipline.
Minimum two years' experience as an ICT Business Analyst, Systems Analyst or similar role.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Experience gathering and documenting business requirements.
Knowledge of business process modelling techniques.
Experience with SQL, databases and reporting tools is desirable.
Understanding of SDLC, Agile and/or Waterfall methodologies.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Strong documentation and presentation abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently.
Desirable
Experience with ERP, CRM or enterprise software platforms.
Knowledge of Microsoft 365, Power BI or business intelligence tools.
Exposure to cloud technologies and API integrations.
Experience within digital transformation or software implementation projects.
What We Offer

Competitive salary package of $80k - 95k

Career development and professional growth opportunities.
Collaborative and supportive work environment.
Opportunity to work on innovative ICT and digital transformation projects.
Flexible working arrangements where applicable.

USVD Consultants Pty Ltd (ACN 666 075 065) ABN: 80 993 362 158 is a recruitment company having office at Bella Vista NSW 2153.

Our client Star Steel Structures & Frames Pty Ltd (SSSF), ABN: 52 630 055 248 located at: 138 Dunheved Cct, St Marys NSW 2760 is a Premier Steel supply and installation company. It is a 100% Australian owned company that provides customisable solutions in high-quality reinforcing mesh, structural steel, and prefabrication services, specializing in eco-friendly construction materials. They focus on delivering durable, moisture-resistant, and heat-resistant products made from 100% recyclable steel. With a commitment to sustainability, Star steel ensures a 48-hour turnaround for quotes while adhering to Australian construction standards. Their products are designed for maximum efficiency and reliability, serving the needs of construction professionals who value quality and eco-conscious solutions.

Due to the business growth and expansion plans, USVD is now looking to recruit a Fitter or maybe two in their Operations team on a permanent full-time basis. The successful candidate will be responsible to fit and assemble fabricated metal parts and mechanical components to install, maintain, and repair machinery and equipment to operational standards, in accordance with technical drawings and safety requirements as per Australian standards.

Position Title: Fitter 
No. of positions: 02
Location: 138 Dunheved Cct, St Marys NSW 2760
Reports to: Operations Head / Supervisor
Annual salary: $80,000 .00 -  $85,000.00 plus Super 

As a Fitter, your main duties and responsibilities include: 

•	Study technical drawings, specifications and job instructions to determine suitable materials, methods, sequence of operations and machine settings.
•	Fit, assemble and align fabricated metal parts and subassemblies to construct or repair machines and mechanical equipment.
•	Check fabricated and assembled metal parts for accuracy, clearance and fit using precision measuring instruments (micrometer, vernier caliper, gauges) etc.
•	Perform precision fitting, levelling and alignment of machines and engineering components.
•	Perform mechanical cutting, machining and general fabrication tasks using hand tools, power tools and fixed/moveable machinery.
•	Carry out shutdown, isolation and lock-out procedures on machines and equipment prior to maintenance or repair work.
•	Use load-shifting equipment (cranes, hoists, forklifts) safely to move materials, machinery and components.
•	Set up, adjust and operate machining tools and equipment for cutting, grinding, drilling, boring and shaping metal stock and castings. 
•	Diagnose faults in mechanical plant, equipment and components, and identify worn or defective parts.
•	Repair, replace and overhaul worn or faulty mechanical components, bearings, drives and transmission assemblies.
•	Install, maintain and repair hydraulic and pneumatic systems and their components, including cutting, threading and bending pipes and lines.
•	Order, select and prepare materials required for fitting, machining and repair tasks.
•	Test and adjust mechanical parts and assemblies after repair to confirm correct operation and performance.
•	Interpret and apply relevant Australian standards, workplace procedures and manufacturer specifications.
•	Work safely with industrial chemicals, materials and equipment in compliance with WHS regulations as per Australian standards.
•	Maintain accurate work records, job sheets and maintenance logs.
•	Communicate and liaise with supervisors, engineers and other trades to coordinate work activities.
•	Provide on-the-job guidance and mentoring to apprentices or junior tradespersons.
•	Participate in environmentally sustainable work practices in the workplace.

Qualification & Licences:
•	Certificate III in Engineering - Mechanical Trade – Fitter (General) preferred.
•	At least 5 years of proven work experience in the above job role. 
•	Sound experience as Fitter in Steel fabrication environment. 
•	Well experienced of WHS requirements, particularly in manufacturing and steel fabrication environment. 
•	Ability to interpret technical drawings, manuals, and specifications.
Skills:
•	Strong organizational and time management skills 
•	Excellent attention to detail 
•	Ability to multitask and physically fit
•	Process and results driven 
•	Team player; collaborative 
•	Resilient, patient and adaptable 
•	Enthusiastic, self-motivated 
•	Proactive & hard-working

Additional information: 
•	Ability to work outside of normal business hours on occasion when delivering key orders. 
•	Ability to travel interstate, if required.

Position: Cabinet Maker
Type: Full-time
Employer: Final Touch Joinery Pty Ltd
Location: Kenthurst NSW 2156
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business:
Final Touch Joinery Pty Ltd is a reputable North-West Sydney-based cabinetry specialist established in 2006 by Director Nathan Diab. With a strong commitment to quality craftsmanship and exceptional customer service, the company specialises in custom kitchen joinery, wardrobes, vanities, and architectural fit-outs for both residential and commercial clients, including high-end homes, unit developments, pubs, clubs, and insurance repair projects. Using premium materials and advanced CAD software, Final Touch Joinery delivers tailored solutions that bring clients’ visions to life with precision, durability, and elegant finishes. The business prides itself on a collaborative, detail-oriented workplace culture where innovation meets traditional joinery skills in a supportive environment focused on excellence and client satisfaction.
About the Position:
The Cabinet Maker plays a vital role in fabricating, assembling, and installing high-quality custom cabinetry, kitchens, wardrobes, and other joinery solutions for Final Touch Joinery’s diverse residential and commercial projects. Working from detailed drawings and client specifications, this position contributes directly to creating functional, beautiful spaces that meet the highest standards of finish and craftsmanship, helping the company maintain its reputation for premium, personalised results in the joinery industry.
Key Responsibilities:
Examining drawings, work orders, and sample parts to determine specifications.
Selecting and working with materials such as timber, veneers, particle board, laminates, and other engineered wood products.
Marking out, cutting, shaping, and assembling components using hand tools, power tools, and computer numerical control (CNC) machines where applicable.
Fabricating and installing kitchen, bathroom, and other cabinetry, wardrobes, counters, and fittings.
Fitting hinges, locks, catches, drawers, shelves, and other hardware with precision.
Ensuring all work meets quality standards, safety requirements, and client expectations.
Collaborating with the team on commercial and residential fit-outs, including repairs and custom solutions.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Minimum Certificate III in Cabinet Making and Installation, Joinery, or any relevant field or at least 2 years of relevant experience.
Minimum 2 years of experience as a cabinet maker or in a related field.
Strong technical skills in reading technical drawings, precise measurement, woodworking machinery operation, and use of hand/power tools.
Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to quality craftsmanship.
Good interpersonal and communication skills to collaborate effectively with team members and understand client requirements.
Physical fitness and ability to work safely in a workshop and on-site environment.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

CQ Sawmilling Pty Ltd, established on 1st March 2022, has taken over the family business of S.T. Olive & Sons. With a legacy of approximately 50 years in Dingo, S.T. Olive & Sons have specialized in supplying timber for both underground and open-cut mining industries and structural hardwood to the wholesale and retail sector. The sawmill has a history of providing “Link n Lock” roofing timber props and other specialized mining timbers to mines in Central Queensland—a service that CQ Sawmilling Pty Ltd intends to continue offering.

We recognise the importance of environmental commitments and will adhere to all relevant environmental laws. We strive to minimise the business's impact on the environment and will take all necessary measures to ensure compliance with environmental authority conditions. Our goal is to generate very little waste at the mills, and any waste produced will be treated appropriately before disposal. Most timber by-products, such as sawdust, woodchips, firewood, and side flitches, are sold to garden suppliers or the general public.

We are seeking highly skilled and experienced Mechanical Technicians to join and work with our team.

Your duties will include but are not limited to:
Maintaining and repairing range of mobile and sawmilling equipment
Conduct root cause analysis, fault-finding and diagnosing efficient solutions to machine breakdowns
